_meta.description: Observable behavior cue -> personality trait mappings, extracted from published research. Effect sizes are reported as-is from source papers; missing r means the source did not give a single numeric correlation (e.g. only qualitative direction or model R^2 reported).
notes: jp_sample: true is reserved for studies actually using Japanese participants. Most cue-trait correlations in the literature are US/EU samples.
Direction of r matters: messy_room has r approx -0.30 with C (i.e. messy = low C).
Where the paper only reports model fit (e.g. PNAS prediction r), the model is the cue->trait predictor, not a single behavior.

cues.note: Openness is the most reliably judged trait from a bedroom; consensus also strong for C (0.42-ish) and E.
Bedrooms reveal very little about Agreeableness; offices essentially nothing (r=-0.04).
Neuroticism is invisible in rooms; raters can't agree.

cues.source: Gosling et al. 2002 (lens model; messy/cluttered cue valid for low C). Direction widely replicated.
cues.note: Specific cue-level r values for cleanliness in original paper are commonly cited around |r|=.20-.35 for C; we did not extract a single canonical r here.

cues.source: Pringle et al. 2021, J Research in Personality (laptop stickers study, N=147 laptops, 8 perceivers)

cues.note: Consensus correlations: E=.44, O=.40, C=.39, A=.28, N=.09. Accuracy (vs self-report) only significant for E and O.

In standardized pose, only E, self-esteem and religiosity judged accurately. In spontaneous pose, accuracy emerged for almost all Big Five. Paper reports lens-model r's; we did not extract single numeric r per trait.
Smile cue drives positive halo: observers rate smiler higher on E, A, O, C, low N. It is also a *valid* cue for E (smile freq correlates with self-rated E).

cues.source: Kachur et al. 2020, Sci Reports (real-life facial images, N approx 12,000)
cues.note: Mean effect size across Big Five = 0.243. C was the most predictable trait from face.
Remaining traits (A, C, N) in 0.17-0.30 range; O and E the strongest.

cues.metric: prediction model r (status text -> self-report O)
cues.source: Schwartz et al. 2013 (PLOS ONE), N approx 75k

cues.note: Open-vocab predictions r=.31 (A, N) to .41 (O). Closed-vocab LIWC r=.21-.29.

cues.source: Schwartz et al. 2013; Mehl et al. 2006 (EAR)
cues.note: Extraverts use party/love-you/boys/ladies; introverts use computer/internet/reading/anime.

cues.source: Schwartz et al. 2013; Park et al. 2015 JPSP
cues.note: 'sick of', 'depressed', 'hate' load on N. Emotionally stable people post about sports, vacation, church.
Network density r=0.52 with one demographic; E correlates with network size and density.

cues.source: Sorokowski et al. 2015 P&ID; Fox & Rooney 2015; meta-analyses
cues.note: Selfies link to grandiose narcissism and self-promotion, especially among men. Effect sizes commonly r=.20-.35.

cues.source: Tanaka et al. 2022, Comput Hum Behav Reports (Japanese undergrads)
cues.note: Japanese sample: Twitter users had lower self-esteem and higher social-comparison orientation than non-users. Instagram users higher in narcissism and self-esteem.

cues.metric: model-level prediction r (median); sociableness facet r=0.40

cues.note: C best predicted by phone activity timing patterns and weather/calendar apps.
Agreeableness essentially not predictable from smartphone behavior at baseline.

cues.source: Mairesse et al. 2007 (J Artif Intell Res, classification accuracy ~73%); Mehl & Pennebaker EAR studies
cues.note: Extraverts: more F0 variation, louder, fewer/shorter silent pauses, more variation in pitch. Quantitative cue-level r not always reported; classification accuracy up to 73%.
E correlates with word count in daily conversation but not in stream-of-consciousness essays. Highly context-dependent.

cues.source: Mehl et al. 2006 (Personality in its natural habitat, JPSP)
cues.note: Frequent swearing -> lower A, lower C, lower O, higher E.

cues.source: Kawashima et al. 2019 (EEG study); Rauthmann et al. 2012 'Eyes as windows to the soul'
cues.note: Mixed literature: original raw r in single studies can reach .73 to -.36; meta-analytically nonverbal-E correlations shrink to r approx .13.

cues.source: Borkenau & Liebler 1992 J Pers Soc Psychol; Naumann 2009

cues.note: Conscientious targets dress in tailored/neutral/structured ways; this cue is *valid* (correlates with self-report C) and *used* by observers.
Watch-wearers self-report higher C and are more punctual.

thin_slice_accuracy._metric: Self-stranger correlation (zero-acquaintance / thin-slice judgment vs self-report)
_sources: Ambady & Rosenthal 1992 meta-analysis (overall effect size r=0.39 for thin-slice predictions across criteria; not Big Five specifically)
Carney, Colvin, Hall 2007 'A thin slice perspective on the accuracy of first impressions'
Vazire 2010 SOKA (round-robin design, 165 targets x friends x strangers)
Borkenau & Liebler 1992 (target variance in zero-acquaintance Big Five)
by_trait_qualitative_ranking_easiest_to_: E (Extraversion) - reliably judged from <5s in Carney 2007; r typically 0.30-0.50 stranger-self
C (Conscientiousness) - moderately judged after 5s; also visible in rooms
O (Openness) - judged best from environments (rooms, laptop stickers) not from short interactions
N (Neuroticism) - poorly visible to strangers; SELF best knows N
A (Agreeableness) - HARDEST to judge from thin slices; needs longer observation

soka_model_summary.agreeableness_C: self-knowledge is poor; others see C and A behaviorally

thin_slice_accuracy.carney_2007_exposure_duration_finding: Negative affect, E, C, and intelligence judged moderately well after 5s. Positive affect, N, O, A need more time. 60s is the optimal cost/accuracy ratio.

japan_specific_evidence._summary: Direct Japanese-sample cue-trait correlation data is scarce. Main usable source: Tanaka et al. 2022 (Comput Hum Behav Reports) on Japanese undergrads' SNS use, and Iwata et al. (W-NUT 2016) on Japanese-text personality estimation. No Japanese replication of Gosling's room study or Mehl EAR work was found in this search.

entries.source: Tanaka, Sakuraya, Asai, Watanabe, Iida 2022 (Comput Hum Behav Reports)
Iwata, Otomo, Asai 2016 (W-NUT, ACL workshop) 'Personality Estimation from Japanese Text'
entries.note: Japanese particle ('joshi') category, unique to Japanese, strongly correlated with several Big Five profiles. No single r reported.

implications_for_checklist: Most observable cues should be assumed cross-culturally transferable but with smaller effect sizes in Japan due to display-rule and modesty norms (e.g. selfie posting absolute frequency is lower in JP than US, but the rank-order link to narcissism likely holds).
Be especially cautious with verbal cues (talkativeness, swearing) -- Japanese conversational norms compress E variance.
Room/desk neatness as a C cue is plausibly *more* informative in Japan because of widespread baseline tidiness norms; deviations stand out.

high_visibility_traits_use_observation: Extraversion (smile, F0 variation, talkativeness, eye contact, calls, network size)
Openness (room/desk decoration variety, laptop stickers, art/music words)
Conscientiousness (formal dress, tidy desk, watch, on-time, scheduling apps)
low_visibility_traits_require_self_repor: Neuroticism (best from self; bedroom consensus r=0.08)
Agreeableness (bedroom r=0.20, office r=-0.04, smartphone r=0.05; need long observation or behavior in conflict situations)
checklist_design_implications.minimum_observation_window: 60s of behavior optimizes accuracy/cost (Carney 2007). <5s is enough only for E and C.
